interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is documented. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 62.79 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 47.09–78.49 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 3.7 and an ISUP grade group 5 Gleason pattern on the prostatectomy specimen. Contributing to risk are the pathological T3a stage and documented extraprostatic extension. Countervailing findings include negative surgical margins, no seminal vesicle invasion, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no detected lymph node metastasis. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy comparison is limited as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report from the initial biopsy are missing. Nodal status was assessed with no metastasis found. Prognostic uncertainty remains due to the lack of postoperative PSA data and follow-up information. Future trajectory assessment would be significantly revised by obtaining serial postoperative PSA measurements and understanding their subsequent patterns. The expected follow-up without an event is 62.8 months, within a heuristic sensitivity range of 47.1 to 78.5 months.
